eisenhower.title: Eisenhower matrix online
eisenhower.intro: Sort your tasks into the four boxes, free and with no sign-up. Everything stays in your browser: print the matrix or pick it up in Cosmo.
eisenhower.privacy: Your tasks are saved in this browser only. Nothing is sent to Cosmo.
eisenhower.ctaTitle: Turn box 2 into real time slots
eisenhower.ctaText: In Cosmo, your important tasks get a slot in the calendar, next to your habits and objectives.
eisenhower.howTitle: How to use the matrix well
eisenhower.how1: Start by emptying your head: every task for the week, without sorting. Then ask two questions of each: does this move me towards my objectives? Does it have to be done today or tomorrow?
eisenhower.how2: The box that matters most is the second one: important but not urgent. That is where the projects that change your quarter live. Give them a slot in your calendar before the week fills up.
eisenhower.moreLink: the Eisenhower matrix explained, with examples

okr.title: Free OKR generator
okr.intro: Write your OKRs in three steps: an area, an objective, then suggested key results you adjust. Free, no sign-up, everything stays in your browser.
okr.step3Hint: Up to 5. Adjust the start and target on the right.
okr.krEmpty: Tick key results on the left.
okr.hintNumber: An objective has no number in it: numbers belong in the key results.
okr.ctaText: In Cosmo, your key results move forward next to the tasks and habits that drive them. The demo opens with this OKR already created.
okr.howTitle: How to write a good OKR
okr.how1: The objective says where you want to go, in words and without numbers. The key results say how you will know you got there: a number, a unit, a starting value and a target you think you have a 50 to 70% chance of hitting.
okr.how2: Two to four key results per objective are enough, over a quarter. Review them for ten minutes every week: that appointment is what makes the difference.

habit.title: Custom printable habit tracker
habit.intro: Pick the month, write your habits, print: your grid is ready to tick. Free, no sign-up, everything stays in your browser.
habit.hint: Start with two or three habits: the grid takes up to eight.
habit.rule: Golden rule: never miss two days in a row.
habit.ctaTitle: Track your habits on your phone too
habit.ctaText: In Cosmo, each habit has its streak, a six-month heatmap and reminders, next to your tasks and objectives.
habit.howTitle: How to use your habit tracker well
habit.how1: Write each habit in its minimal version ("ten minutes of reading" rather than "read for an hour") and attach it to a specific moment of your day.
habit.how2: Keep the sheet where you will see it and tick right away. At the end of the month, look at the days that slip and change a single thing for next month.

planner.title: Weekly planner online
planner.intro: Fill the grid block by block: deep work, meetings, breaks. Free, no sign-up, everything stays in your browser.
planner.hint: Click a slot and type the planned block.
planner.ctaTitle: Place your real tasks in the calendar
planner.ctaText: In Cosmo, your tasks slide into the calendar as time slots, next to your habits and objectives.
planner.howTitle: How to fill your week well
planner.how1: Start with deep work blocks, at the hours when you work best, then group meetings and calls into one stretch.
planner.how2: Keep a buffer every day: a plan filled to the minute is wrong by Tuesday. Each evening, adjust the next day in ten minutes.

pomodoro.title: Online Pomodoro timer
pomodoro.intro: 25 minutes on a single task, a 5-minute break, a long break every four sessions. Free, no sign-up.
pomodoro.ctaTitle: Link your sessions to your priorities
pomodoro.ctaText: In Cosmo, the task at hand comes from your prioritised list and your calendar, next to your objectives.
pomodoro.howTitle: How to get the most from the Pomodoro method
pomodoro.how1: One session, one task. If an idea or a request comes up, write it down and get back to the task: you will handle it at the break.
pomodoro.how2: During the break, step away from the screen. After four sessions, take the long break: it is what keeps you going all day.
